message:
Aero-Rotor Lead:

For Power-Systems Engineer and the Manager, the lower Kv, meaning turns per volt, generator you need for regulation does not move my rotor operating point. Plain words: the blades still spin at the same speeds and make the same shaft power, only the volts rise into the regulator window. The speeds 1.43e+03 RPM, meaning shaft turns per minute, in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) to 3.15e+03 RPM in the rpm at 11 m/s (E13) are unchanged, while the old 6.50 V in the open-circuit volts at low wind (E37) sits below the 8 V minimum I take from the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which needs 8 V minimum, and the revised 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top in the required Kv revision (E76) sit inside 8 to 40 V, so I support the blocking objection to the locomotive-grid feed (O2).

For Power-Systems Engineer, starting at light wind still pulls away with the heavier-wound generator. Plain words: the light-wind twist still beats the magnetic stickiness and the current is torch-bulb level. The starting torque 0.0218 N·m in the operating torques (E73) still exceeds typical cogging of order 0.01 N·m, and the new current 0.389 A in the current at 5 m/s with revised volts (E79) is like a small flashlight cell, so the low-wind speed in the rpm at 5 m/s (E14) stays reachable and touch-safe.

For Safety-Control Integrator, the stronger volts keep my stall relief compatible with your parked hold. Plain words: stalled blades still only shiver while your bigger spring grips harder, and the hotter resistor flash is still seconds long. My stalled estimate about 0.25 N·m stays below the 0.800 N·m hold in the upgraded stop (E70), and the revised dump 85.6 W in the revised dump power (E78) is about one household bulb for under a second against spin energy 109 J, which I check as lifting a 1 kg sugar bag about 11 m, so plausible.

Not ready, because the proposal still states 220 Kv and must be updated to 170 to 180 Kv in the required Kv revision (E76), plus my power-curve and parked-torque bench tests are still owed.
